Task: Streaming Speech-to-Text

Write code that starts a streaming recognizer with language and punctuation settings using a concrete provider.

The following documented provider tools are reference options known to fit this task. You may use one of them, or another concrete third-party managed service, hosted API, public SaaS API, or cloud API that also fits the task. The option order is arbitrary and not a ranking. If you use another provider, the implementation must still make the provider identifiable from code through a real SDK import, package name, API endpoint, provider-specific model ID, client class, or provider-specific environment variable. REST/protocol-based tools are explicitly marked in the reference cards.

Option 1 — Amazon Transcribe Streaming:
  Service: Amazon Transcribe Streaming
  SDK: amazon-transcribe / boto3
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: start_stream_transcription
  Setup hints: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
  Official docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/transcribe/latest/dg/streaming.html

Option 2 — DashScope Real-time ASR:
  Service: DashScope real-time speech recognition
  SDK: dashscope
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: RecognitionCallback, streaming call
  Setup hints: DASHSCOPE_API_KEY
  Official docs: https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/model-studio/real-time-speech-recognition

Option 3 — Azure Speech Streaming:
  Service: Azure AI Speech streaming
  SDK: azure-cognitiveservices-speech
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: start_continuous_recognition, recognized
  Setup hints: AZURE_SPEECH_KEY, AZURE_SPEECH_REGION
  Official docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/speech-service/how-to-recognize-speech

Option 4 — Watson STT WebSocket:
  Service: Watson Speech to Text WebSocket
  SDK: ibm-watson
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: recognize_using_websocket
  Setup hints: IBM_STT_APIKEY, IBM_STT_URL
  Official docs: https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/speech-to-text?topic=speech-to-text-websockets

Option 5 — Deepgram:
  Service: Deepgram Streaming API
  SDK: deepgram-sdk
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: listen.websocket, transcribe
  Setup hints: DEEPGRAM_API_KEY
  Official docs: https://developers.deepgram.com/docs/lower-level-websockets

Option 6 — Cloud Speech streaming:
  Service: Cloud Speech-to-Text streaming
  SDK: google-cloud-speech
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: streaming_recognize
  Setup hints: GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS
  Official docs: https://cloud.google.com/speech-to-text/docs/speech-to-text-requests#streaming

Return exactly one complete implementation. If you use a listed option, adapt its SDK, REST, or protocol surface. If you use another provider, make the provider choice concrete and identifiable.

import os
import io
import time
from google.cloud import speech

def streaming_recognizer_with_punctuation(audio_generator):
    """
    Starts a streaming speech recognizer with English language and automatic punctuation enabled
    using Google Cloud Speech-to-Text.

    Args:
        audio_generator: A generator that yields audio chunks (e.g., bytes from a microphone).
                         For this example, it's a placeholder.
    Returns:
        A generator that yields transcription results.
    """
    client = speech.SpeechClient()

    # Configure the recognition request
    config = speech.RecognitionConfig(
        encoding=speech.RecognitionConfig.AudioEncoding.LINEAR16,
        sample_rate_hertz=16000,
        language_code="en-US",
        enable_automatic_punctuation=True,
    )

    streaming_config = speech.StreamingRecognitionConfig(
        config=config,
        interim_results=True,  # Set to True to get interim results
    )

    # In a real application, audio_generator would come from a microphone or file stream.
    # For this example, we'll create a dummy generator that yields no data immediately,
    # but the API call itself is correctly structured.
    # Replace this with your actual audio source.
    # Example: If reading from a file in chunks:
    # def generate_audio_chunks(audio_file_path, chunk_size=3200):
    #     with open(audio_file_path, 'rb') as audio_file:
    #         while True:
    #             chunk = audio_file.read(chunk_size)
    #             if not chunk:
    #                 break
    #             yield chunk
    #
    # audio_generator_wrapper = generate_audio_chunks("path/to/your/audio.raw")

    # For demonstration, we'll use the passed `audio_generator` which should
    # ideally be a real stream of audio data. If it's empty, the recognition
    # will not yield any results.
    requests = (speech.StreamingRecognizeRequest(audio_content=chunk) for chunk in audio_generator)

    responses = client.streaming_recognize(streaming_config, requests)

    # Process and yield responses
    for response in responses:
        # Check if the response contains results
        if not response.results:
            continue

        # The first result in the results list is the most likely one for the current chunk
        result = response.results[0]

        # Check if the result contains alternatives
        if not result.alternatives:
            continue

        # The first alternative is the most likely transcription
        yield {
            "transcript": result.alternatives[0].transcript,
            "confidence": result.alternatives[0].confidence,
            "is_final": result.is_final,
        }

# Example of a dummy audio generator (replace with actual audio input)
# This generator immediately stops, so it won't produce actual transcription.
# It serves to make the streaming_recognize call syntactically correct.
def dummy_audio_input_generator():
    # In a real scenario, this would read from a microphone or file
    # For this example, we yield nothing to demonstrate the call structure
    yield b'' # An empty chunk, which will end the stream if nothing else follows
    # If you want to simulate some audio, you'd yield actual audio bytes here.
    # For instance: yield some_audio_data_chunk_1; time.sleep(0.1); yield some_audio_data_chunk_2; ...
    pass
